harties Hyacinth

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Harties is in trouble again as million of hyacinth plants spread across its surface. So why did water affairs cancel a programme that was finally working

Unique Selling Point:
GREAT VISUALS ON THE DAM AND AN INSIDE TAKE ON ANOTHER MURKY TENDER PROCESS - AN EXCELLENT NARRATIVE AND VISUALS FROM CARTE BLANCHE IN 2009

Summary:
Is there a problem with the water I asked the people at Magalies golf course on the Magalies River.
“Is there a problem with the water?” they repeated. THERE IS A BIG PROBLEM! You can’t even see the river. There is so much hyacinth it looks like a lawn that you can walk on!

For ten years the dam has been slowly improving, driven by a bio remediation scheme and the passion of a water affairs scientist Mr Petrus Venter. But last year the department of water affairs pulled the plug on the project and the result is that masses of microsystis is now recolonizing the surface of the dam. Next will come the blue green algae. And the stench.



Further information:
Ten years ago the project called Metsi A me was approved at ministerial level. Rand water was the implementing agent and Petrus Venter from Water affairs at Hartebeespoort ran the programme.

It employed 110 people. They would go out on boats and remove huge quantities of the hyancinth with big booms like curtains, take the stuff across the road to a viviculture farm where it became compost. They initiated a fishing project to remove alien fish species like barbell and carp that stir up the blue green rotting algae at the bottom, and sold them for R10 per kilogram on a coupon system.
Then they started dredging the sediment from the river to grow bulbs in with Hadeco and some of the sediment was used for brickmaking. With all the development the reeds on the banks were removed destroying the natural filtration of the dam, so instead Metsi A me built huge floating islands that have had international acclaim. Then the bird started coming back. Instead of a couple of hundred birds, Birdlife Africa John Wesson was counting thousands. The flamingos returned.

The idea says Petrus is that if you take a biological approach you can clean the dam and youdon’t have to spray chemicals and destroy the ecosystem. “A one kilogram bird will have a multiple effect on the dam. That is the absolute power of a biological programme” says Petrus.

MARLENE ? worked as the communications person for the programme for several years.. She says that it was starting to show results and there was a 150% difference. In winter the dam would stay clearer and clearer for longer. She says Petrus was a slave driver and he had a one track vision but he could account for every cent that was spent.

That may have been the problem says Petrus. He ran the project on a shoestring of R50 million that he stretched out over four years. Getting the funding each year was extremely stressful and that in itself he said was a major achievement.

According to a civil engineering journal, during its heyday the programme employed between 80 and 140 workers and removed at least 64 000m² of hyacinths, 2 400 tons of litter and debris and 31 million litres of algae soup.




Recently the department announced that they had R254 million rand to spend and Petrus knew the writing was on the wall. Tenderpreneurs were after the funds. “ I asked inconvenient questions” says Petrus. Soon after the money was announced, his bosses cancelled the programme and began to sideline him. In March last year Water affairs pulled the plug.

To give you an analogy says Petrus. “ There are potholes in the streets in Madibeng. Some people have tried to fix them at their own cost. But then the police will come and say you aren’t allowed to fix the pothole. The reason is that they want to reserve the work for someone else who really just wants the money. The situation with Metsi A me is similar.”

“ I still want to play a role but they will do anything to get rid of me from Harties.”
Now he fears tenderpreneurs are going to come in and just spray with poisonous chemicals destroying ten years of work.

Meanwhile sewerage spillages are a constant threat and in the heat of the summer the Hyancinth is multiplying exponentially.

Press Release:


Harties Hyacinth
Floating on the surface of a river or dam, water hyacinth seems a pretty plant with a purple flower. But it is in fact one of the world’s most invasive and rapidly proliferating aquatic weeds. For ten years the Department of Water and Sanitation had nurtured their programme to keep the hyacinth and algae at bay on the Hartbeespoort dam, but last year they pulled the plug. Now, millions of these plants have taken over Gauteng’s Magalies River blocking it entirely in areas. Carte Blanche gets onto the dam and wades into the controversy in search of answers.


Script:


HARTIES HYACINTH FINAL SCRIPT TX SUNDAY 19th FEB 2017

Commentary one
If you have ever thought you could walk on water, the Magalies River that runs into Hartbeespoort dam might be a good place to start.

LINK
It’s really hard to believe that this is a river – three months ago the cruise barge operating ……now they are literally high and dry

Derek
Well Muis this is like a luxuriant pasture not Water world?!
Muis
Derek this is crazy, this is where we are now we might just use this to extend our golf course

Commentary Two
Muis Lombard is manager of Magalies Park, on the edge of the Magalies River. The resort’s attraction, is its proximity to the river, a river no longer visible from the air.

Muis
The community is up in arms, the shore owners are up in arms, people affected along this river are up in arms. We are all losing business!

Upsound hyacinth eating machine

Commentary Three
Magalies park spent R200 000 on this machine to chop and remove the hyacinth, but after a while Muis just gave up. This free floating aquatic plant which can double every 11 to 18 days and starves the water of oxygen, had won the battle for the river - now stretching almost 6kilometres up stream.

Muis
I can’t do weddings anymore because this is what you get as a backdrop in your wedding photo
No romantic cruise
Not at all

LINK
The hyacinth is growing back with a vengeance on Hartbeespoort dam. Speak to the locals and they blame the department for pulling the plug on their own apparently successful project to clean up the dam

Commentary four
It was called Metsi a me, a priority programme instituted ten years ago by the then water affairs. This biological remedy employed over a hundred people. Rand water was the implementing agent, and Petrus Venter spearheaded the programme on the ground for the department

PETRUS
I am focusing on the whole food web, so if you have one link missing the whole web collapses and that is the state of the dam, and if you bring in all these components some magic happens

Commentary five
The magic didn’t happen overnight. There are 47 sewage works releasing water of varying qualities into the three rivers that feed the dam. This was the Hennops River this week. The foam indicates a sewage spill

Petrus
So we have to start with a programme of controlling this impacts, having control booms on the dam at the dam wall, different set of it – if the wind brings in algae, hyacinth, the debris we constructively contain it and remove it

Commentary Six
The development along the shorelines had destroyed the vegetation that filters the water, so Metsi A me built floating wetlands to replace that function. Then they introduced a fishing project to reduce the bottom feeders like carp and barbell that stir up algae. Marlene Mackay worked for Metsi A Mi for nearly three years.

MARLENE
And that whole fishing team consisted of about 60 people who fished every day, and the fish was then sold back to the public for absolutely no money

Commentary Seven
The hyacinth they removed was turned into compost at a vermiculture farm, across the road from the dam. As the years progressed, Metsi A Mi became a showcase for the department

Do you think Metsi A mi really worked?
Marlene
Absolutely! we measured it according to clear water status. Initially when I started with the project the clear water status would be until winter ends july August …by the last year on the project we saw clear water till November December. Clear Clear water with healthy filamentous algae in that water , no hyacinth on the dam, the greater dam basin looked incredible.

Commentary eight
By 2012 they had removed 64 000 cubic metres of hyacinth, 2400 tonnes of litter and debris, 31 000 million litres of algal soup, and more than 190 tonnes of unwanted fish species. They had rehabilitated 8530 square metres of shoreline and established nearly 5000 square metres of floating wetlands, all scrounged from a budget of around R22 million a year.



DEREK LINK .
It wasn’t smooth sailing but after a decade the water was getting clearer for longer after each season, but that didn’t seem to matter to the department

Commentary nine
And in March last year they pulled the plug. About 120 people lost their jobs almost overnight. Ronald Baloyi worked on the programme for eight years .

Derek
Why do you think the department suddenly stopped the project?
Ronald
I asked some of the questions. I never got the answer that satisfied me, because they talk about the availability of funds, they talk about they were not having the money to run the project

Commentary Ten
Ronald is hoping another programme will begin soon.

Ronald Baloyi
The progress of my life it’s a total stop, because I am no longer generating anything for my family or my life.

Commentary eleven
Departmental spokesman Sputnik Ratau informally told Carte Blanche Metsi A mi was dead. Petrus Venter says there are new plans in the pipeline

Derek
Would you agree the plans are rather confused
Petrus
Well I don’t think with all the knowledge and experience there is confusion. It’s the departments processes – the procurement aspect is very tedious.
Derek
So while they prevaricate the hyacinth grows across the dam?
Petrus
That is true, but I believe that if there is political intervention the HARTIES METSI A Mi CAN be revitalized in a very short space of time

Commentary twelve
But our understanding is that is not going to happen. Instead it seems a private sector solution may be sought by the department. In the meantime, evidence of rat tailed maggots in the hyacinth, has emerged. These maggots are attracted to sewerage

Derek
When you look at the dam now how do you feel?
Petrus
A bit heartbroken

Commentary thirteen
Heartbreak, frustration and anger are whipping around the dam. At the top of the cableway, we met Iain Gunn. A man, with a fiery enthusiasm for tourism.

Iain
The biggest problem is hyacinth and there is no plan in place from government to do something now
Derek
They say there is a project
Iain
There is a plan on paper – it will go down to another 20 – 30 meetings by that time this whole beautiful dam we see behind us will be one big patch of beautiful green lawn

Commentary fourteen
The hyacinth moves with the wind. Each plant can produce thousands of seeds and these seeds can remain viable for more than 28 years. Now estates close to the Magalies River are literally hemmed in and boat access is almost impossible.

LINK
Its one thing to be shocked by the amount of hyacinth but its science that reveals the devastation – its called the quack count and this year there hasn’t been much quacking

Commentary fifteen
For the last seven years these citizen scientists have been counting aquatic birds on the dam, in collaboration with the university of Cape Town.

Up sound
Green back Heron

Commentary sixteen
John Wesson is a senior manager at Wessa. As Metsi A mi progressed he says the birdlife returned.

John
and we started seeing results over time and you can see what has happened since it was stopped we are having a total crash around the dam as far as the hyacinth goes

Commentary seventeen
At the end of January five teams of bird counters traversed the dam.

Up sound
Two more purple heron

They had lasted counted birds in July 2016, only a few months after Metsi A mi had ended. This year they got a shock.

John
Worst we have seen it so far– changed the habit quite drastically closing up the shoreline and blocking the river and that has changed the habitat for lots of birds especially wader type species, the large numbers of flamingos gone

Commentary eighteen
It wasn’t just the flamingos. Their last count had recorded 11 860 birds, by January this year that number had diminished to 3462

DEREK LINK
Our questions are not that difficult why was Metsi A mi stopped? What will replace it and when, but the department has refused to comment or grant us an interview

Commentary nineteen
What we do know can be found in this letter from the minister sent in July last year to the DA:

“The department is in the process of procurement as for the next three years, the programme has been allocated a dedicated budet.

Commentary twenty
Seven months later nothing has happened.

Marlene
I hear now that there is talk of residents spraying and taking matters into their own hands. If you kill the hyacinth, it will sink to the bottom of the dam and it will just nutrient charge it all over again and in two years we will sit with a dam that is covered in blue green algae.

Commentary Twenty
But will the department even be able to come up with the money they have committed? Last week an expose in the City Press announced the Department of Water and Sanitation is bankrupt. The department has denied the allegations. Meanwhile back on the dam, the hyacinth is multiplying.

THE END Duration: 10 min 03.












PROMO ONE 10 seconds
Residents around Hartbeespoort dam are waging a war against hyacinth
Muis
I can’t do weddings anymore because this is what you get as a backdrop in your wedding photo

PROMO TWO
The department of Water and sanitation pulled the plug on their own clean up of Hartbeespoort dam. Now the birdlife is disappearing.

John Wesson
you can see what happened now its stopped, and we ahre having a total crash around the dam as far as the hyacinth goes.


PROMO THREE
Water hyacinth is out of control on Hartbeespoort dam, and residents are angry.

Iain
There is a plan on paper – it will go down to another 20 – 30 meetings by that time this whole beautiful dam we see behind us will be one big patch of beautiful green lawn

metadata.Unique Selling Point: GREAT VISUALS ON THE DAM AND AN INSIDE TAKE ON ANOTHER MURKY TENDER PROCESS - AN EXCELLENT NARRATIVE AND VISUALS FROM CARTE BLANCHE IN 2009
metadata.Summary: Is there a problem with the water I asked the people at Magalies golf course on the Magalies River. “Is there a problem with the water?” they repeated. THERE IS A BIG PROBLEM! You can’t even see the river. There is so much hyacinth it looks like a lawn that you can walk on! For ten years the dam has been slowly improving, driven by a bio remediation scheme and the passion of a water affairs scientist Mr Petrus Venter. But last year the department of water affairs pulled the plug on the project and the result is that masses of microsystis is now recolonizing the surface of the dam. Next will come the blue green algae. And the stench.
metadata.Further information: Ten years ago the project called Metsi A me was approved at ministerial level. Rand water was the implementing agent and Petrus Venter from Water affairs at Hartebeespoort ran the programme. It employed 110 people. They would go out on boats and remove huge quantities of the hyancinth with big booms like curtains, take the stuff across the road to a viviculture farm where it became compost. They initiated a fishing project to remove alien fish species like barbell and carp that stir up the blue green rotting algae at the bottom, and sold them for R10 per kilogram on a coupon system. Then they started dredging the sediment from the river to grow bulbs in with Hadeco and some of the sediment was used for brickmaking. With all the development the reeds on the banks were removed destroying the natural filtration of the dam, so instead Metsi A me built huge floating islands that have had international acclaim. Then the bird started coming back. Instead of a couple of hundred birds, Birdlife Africa John Wesson was counting thousands. The flamingos returned. The idea says Petrus is that if you take a biological approach you can clean the dam and youdon’t have to spray chemicals and destroy the ecosystem. “A one kilogram bird will have a multiple effect on the dam. That is the absolute power of a biological programme” says Petrus. MARLENE ? worked as the communications person for the programme for several years.. She says that it was starting to show results and there was a 150% difference. In winter the dam would stay clearer and clearer for longer. She says Petrus was a slave driver and he had a one track vision but he could account for every cent that was spent. That may have been the problem says Petrus. He ran the project on a shoestring of R50 million that he stretched out over four years. Getting the funding each year was extremely stressful and that in itself he said was a major achievement. According to a civil engineering journal, during its heyday the programme employed between 80 and 140 workers and removed at least 64 000m² of hyacinths, 2 400 tons of litter and debris and 31 million litres of algae soup. Recently the department announced that they had R254 million rand to spend and Petrus knew the writing was on the wall. Tenderpreneurs were after the funds. “ I asked inconvenient questions” says Petrus. Soon after the money was announced, his bosses cancelled the programme and began to sideline him. In March last year Water affairs pulled the plug. To give you an analogy says Petrus. “ There are potholes in the streets in Madibeng. Some people have tried to fix them at their own cost. But then the police will come and say you aren’t allowed to fix the pothole. The reason is that they want to reserve the work for someone else who really just wants the money. The situation with Metsi A me is similar.” “ I still want to play a role but they will do anything to get rid of me from Harties.” Now he fears tenderpreneurs are going to come in and just spray with poisonous chemicals destroying ten years of work. Meanwhile sewerage spillages are a constant threat and in the heat of the summer the Hyancinth is multiplying exponentially. PARTICIPANTS PETRUS VENTER SPUTNIK RATAU MARLENE ??
